literal: Deposed Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling; Deposed Emperor Houfei, Prince of Anding; Emperor Chu, Prince of Pingyang.
idiomatic: Deposed Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling; Deposed Emperor Houfei, Prince of Anding; Emperor Chu, Prince of Pingyang.

literal: The Deposed Emperor Qianfei bore the taboo name Gong, styled Xiuye; he was the son of Prince of Guangling Hui, Yu; his mother was Lady Wang.
idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor Qianfei bore the taboo name Gong, styled Xiuye. He was the son of Prince of Guangling Hui, Yu; his mother was Lady Wang.

literal: In youth he was upright and careful, with purpose and measure.
idiomatic: As a boy he was upright and careful, with steadiness of purpose.

literal: When grown he loved learning, and was famed for filial service to his grandmother and principal mother.
idiomatic: When he came of age he loved learning and was famed for filial devotion to his grandmother and principal mother.

literal: In the Zhengshi era he inherited the princely fief.
idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he inherited the princely title.

literal: In the Yanchang era he was appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant.
idiomatic: In the Yanchang era he was made direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant.

literal: In the Shengui era he was advanced to concurrent scattered cavalier attendant.
idiomatic: In the Shengui era he was advanced to concurrent scattered cavalier attendant.

literal: In the second year of Zhengguang he was regular attendant and concurrently chief of the yellow-gate secretariat.
idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang he became regular attendant and concurrently chief of the yellow-gate secretariat.

literal: Because the emperor saw Yuan Cha monopolizing power, he then pleaded illness and would not attend court.
idiomatic: Seeing Yuan Cha monopolize power, the prince pleaded illness and stopped attending court.

literal: After a long while he took refuge in muteness.
idiomatic: After a long while he feigned muteness.

literal: In the fifth year he was appointed in situ grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, [1] with the additional title of scattered cavalier attendant.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he was given the post of grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, [1] and the additional title of scattered cavalier attendant.

literal: In the first year of Jianyi he was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyi he was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: The prince had ceased speech and was approaching a full twelve-year cycle; he dwelt at Longhua Temple and had no dealings with others.
idiomatic: The prince had not spoken for nearly twelve years. He lived at Longhua Temple and kept no company outside it.

literal: At the end of Yongan someone informed Emperor Xiaozhuang that the prince’s silence betokened a different design;
idiomatic: Late in Yongan someone told Emperor Xiaozhuang that the prince’s silence hid treasonous intent;

literal: among the people wandering talk also said there was the aura of a Son of Heaven.
idiomatic: and street rumor claimed the aura of a true emperor clung to him.

literal: The prince, fearing disaster, fled and hid at Shangluo; soon he was pursued and seized, sent to the capital, imprisoned many days, and released for lack of evidence.
idiomatic: Fearing ruin, the prince fled to Shangluo; pursuers soon caught him and brought him to the capital. After many days in custody he was released—for nothing could be proved.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang died, Erzhu Shilong and others, because Yuan Ye was remote in kinship and not what men’s hopes pushed forward, saw in the prince’s hidden silence and retiring body a measure beyond others; they plotted to depose and install, feared he truly would not speak, and so had those close to the prince convey their intent, and also pressed him by force.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang died, Erzhu Shilong and his faction found Yuan Ye too remote in blood and too little esteemed to hold the throne. The prince’s long silence and retiring life seemed to hide uncommon depth; they resolved on a change of ruler. Fearing he would never break silence, they sent intimates to explain their wish—and backed the message with threats.

literal: The prince then answered: "Does Heaven speak?"
idiomatic: The prince answered at last: "Does Heaven speak?"

literal: Shilong and the rest were greatly pleased.
idiomatic: Shilong and the others were overjoyed.

literal: Spring, second month, day jisi: Ye advanced to the south of Mang; Shilong and the rest received the prince outside the eastern suburb and performed the rite of abdication; the hundred officials submitted a memorial saying: "Decline and peace follow the times; deep sorrow opens the sage—thus the six dragons are in the saddle and the three stones rise as tokens."
idiomatic: In spring of the second month, on jisi day, Yuan Ye advanced to the south of Mang. Shilong and his party received the prince outside the eastern suburb and performed the abdication rite. The hundred officials memorialized: "Fortune and misfortune turn with the age; grave peril summons the sage—thus the six dragons take the reins and the three stones bear heaven’s mandate."

literal: We bow and consider that Your Majesty’s fortune belongs to a thousand ages, wisdom encompasses the ten thousand things, alone you illumine the attached images, subtly you reach heaven and man; the precious succession has its place, glorious dwelling is yours—yet you would rest in solitary good and not pursue universal aid; the numinous mandate lingers, dark and bright alike wait.
idiomatic: We humbly consider that Your Majesty’s fate spans a thousand ages and your wisdom embraces all things beneath heaven; you alone illumine the patterns of the Changes and penetrate the border of heaven and humanity. The sacred succession is yours, the bright dwelling rightly yours—yet you would keep to private good and refuse the common weal; the numinous charge still hesitates, and both realms of the living and the dead stand waiting.

literal: We pray that you timely follow the songs of the people, think on this ancestral temple, lay aside weariness and illness, and truly answer man and spirit.
idiomatic: We beg you to heed the people’s song, remember the ancestral shrine, put aside fatigue and sickness, and answer both men and spirits as heaven demands.

literal: The prince answered: "Measuring my slight person, I therefore yielded the charge."
idiomatic: The prince replied: "Knowing how slight I am, I yielded the throne."

literal: Yet the kings and dukes were earnest to the utmost; one could not refuse and disobey.
idiomatic: But the princes and ministers pressed with such zeal that refusal was impossible.

literal: Now I respectfully accept what you have set forth—only ashamed that I cannot bear the burden."
idiomatic: I accept in reverence what you urge—ashamed only that I am unfit to bear so great a weight."

literal: Grand Preceptor Erzhu Dulu presented the imperial seal and cord and robes of investiture; he then mounted the carriage; the hundred officials attended in guard; he entered by the Jianchun and Yunlong gates, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate in the front palace, and the hundred officials bowed in congratulation.
idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Erzhu Dulu presented seal, cord, and robes of state. The prince mounted the imperial carriage; officials formed his escort. He entered through the Jianchun and Yunlong gates, ascended the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and the court bowed in congratulation.

literal: When the rites were done he ascended the Changhe Gate and issued an edict: "We, with meager virtue, hold the myriad realms in care; we think to share this blessed peace with the hundred millions."
idiomatic: The rites finished, he mounted the Changhe Gate and proclaimed: "We, of little merit, now rule the myriad lands; we mean to share this blessed peace with all the people."

literal: A general amnesty may be declared throughout the realm; Wei is made Great Wei; the second year of Jianming is changed to the first year of Putai.
idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty; Wei shall be Great Wei; the second year of Jianming becomes the first year of Putai.

literal: Offices taxing markets and taxing salt may all be abolished.
idiomatic: All offices that taxed markets and salt are abolished.

literal: Households of miscellaneous trades were lent commoner status for names; official posts remained as before.
idiomatic: Miscellaneous-trade households were granted commoner standing in name; their official assignments stayed unchanged.

literal: The realm’s levy in silk: four hundred bolts per household.
idiomatic: The empire’s silk levy was set at four hundred bolts per household.

literal: Civil and military within and without: a universal promotion of four ranks;
idiomatic: Civil and military officers at court and in the provinces alike received a universal promotion of four ranks;

literal: those in combined seniority whose rank was not yet fixed also received rank.
idiomatic: and those awaiting formal rank in combined seniority were also given a step.

literal: Those struck from the rolls and dismissed from office were specially restored to original salary; noble rank and fief remained as before.
idiomatic: Men struck from the rolls or dismissed from office were restored to their former salaries; titles and fiefs stood unchanged.

literal: Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong, Prince of Changshan Erzhu Dulu, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies Prince of Qi, Duke Xianwu Huan, and the officers and soldiers under Commander Husi Chun—all received a universal promotion of six ranks."
idiomatic: Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong, Prince of Changshan Erzhu Dulu, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, and the troops under Commander Husi Chun were all raised six ranks."

literal: day gengwu: an edict said: "We, with slight person, preside above kings and dukes; evening and dawn we are reverently anxious, as if treading on ice in a ravine."
idiomatic: On gengwu day an edict said: "We, a slight man, sit above kings and dukes; from dusk to dawn we live in reverent fear, as though walking a gorge of ice."

literal: Relying on the spirits of the seven temples and the loyal exertions of the hundred ministers, we may perhaps escape ruin.
idiomatic: By the seven temples’ spirits and the hundred ministers’ loyalty we may yet escape ruin.

literal: The Three Sovereigns were called "emperor" in one way, the Five Thearchs "thearch," the Three Dynasties "king"—each in turn modestly yielded.
idiomatic: The Three Sovereigns were called huang, the Five Thearchs di, the Three Dynasties wang—each age modestly held back the grander title.

literal: From the end of Qin onward all vied to be huangdi—emperor.
idiomatic: From Qin’s fall onward all contended for the title of emperor.

literal: They forgot the deep calamity of bearing what their virtue could not sustain and bequeathed greedy baseness to ten thousand generations.
idiomatic: They forgot the catastrophe of a burden their virtue could not bear and passed greedy folly down through ten thousand generations.

literal: That we now call ourselves emperor is already praise enough!
idiomatic: That we even call ourselves emperor is already more honor than we deserve!

literal: Let this be proclaimed everywhere so all may know."
idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm."

literal: That month Pacifying-the-Distance General Cui Zuchi of Qinghe gathered more than a hundred thousand men from seven commanderies of Qing Province and besieged Dongyang.
idiomatic: That month Cui Zuchi of Qinghe, pacifying-the-distance general, raised more than a hundred thousand men from seven Qing commanderies and besieged Dongyang.

literal: Regional Inspector of You Province Liu Lingzhu raised troops at Ji.
idiomatic: Liu Lingzhu, regional inspector of You, raised troops at Ji.

literal: Pacification-General Gao Gan’ou, grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord and concurrent attendant, Hebei grand envoy, and his younger brother Pacifier of the North, direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant Aocao, led troops by night to surprise Ji Province, seized Regional Inspector Yuan Yi, killed Supervising General Sun Baiyao, and together set up former Administrator of Henei Feng Longzhi to handle provincial affairs.
idiomatic: Gao Gan’ou, pacification-general, grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, concurrent attendant, and Hebei grand envoy, with his younger brother Aocao, pacifier of the north and direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant, led a night raid on Ji Province, seized Yuan Yi the inspector, killed supervising general Sun Baiyao, and installed former Henei administrator Feng Longzhi to govern the province.

literal: Third month, day guiyou: Prince of Changgung Ye was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.
idiomatic: On guiyou day in the third month Prince of Changgung Ye was made prince of Donghai.

literal: An edict made Grand Preceptor, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Qing Province, and Prince of Lu Commandery Su return to the post of grand preceptor;
idiomatic: An edict restored Grand Preceptor Su, grand general of agile cavalry, regional inspector of Qing, and prince of Lu commandery, to grand preceptor;

literal: Special Advance, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Prince of Pei Commandery Xin was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Si Province, and his fief was changed to Prince of Huaiyang;
idiomatic: Xin, special advance, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and prince of Pei, was made grand tutor and governor of Si, with his fief changed to Huaiyang;

literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Regional Inspector of Xu Province, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Regional Inspector of Yong Province, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang—both were made grand generals;
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan, prince of Pengcheng, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Xu, and Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, grand general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Yong, were both made grand generals;

literal: Pillar Grand General, Regional Inspector of Bing Province, Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao was made Pillar of Heaven Grand General;
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, pillar grand general, regional inspector of Bing, and prince of Yingchuan, was made pillar of heaven grand general;

literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, General of the Left Guard, Grand Commander, Regional Inspector of Jin Province, and Duke of Pingyang Commandery with an open state, Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, was enfeoffed Prince of Bohai, fief increased by five hundred households;
idiomatic: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, grand general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, general of the left guard, grand commander, regional inspector of Jin, and state-founding duke of Pingyang commandery, was enfeoffed prince of Bohai with five hundred added households;

literal: Special Advance, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Qinghe Dan was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies;
idiomatic: Dan, prince of Qinghe, special advance and grand general of chariots and cavalry, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies;

literal: Attendant, Grand Tutor, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong was made Grand Guardian;
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, prince of Leping, attendant, grand tutor, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand guardian;

literal: Commissioner with Full Powers, former Minister over the Masses Changsun Zhi was made Grand Preceptor and recorder of Secretariat affairs;
idiomatic: Changsun Zhi, commissioner with full powers and former minister over the masses, was made grand preceptor and recorder of secretariat affairs;

literal: Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Chen, prince of Zhao commandery, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, was made minister of works.

literal: Zhi firmly declined; soon he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Zhi declined firmly; soon he was made grand general of agile cavalry and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day bingzi: the emperor received in audience Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo and the imperial clan at the Xianyang Hall and comforted and exhorted them.
idiomatic: On bingzi day the emperor received Yuan Luo, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, and the imperial clan at Xianyang Hall and exhorted them with words of comfort.

literal: day dingchou: Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Regional Inspector of North Hua Gongsun Lue was given the additional title Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On dingchou day Gongsun Lue, grand general of agile cavalry and regional inspector of North Hua, was given the additional title equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day jimao: an edict ordered General of the Right Guard Heba Sheng together with one person from the Masters of Writing to recruit performers and miscellaneous households for the campaign; on formal entry to service all were given substantive office; those with private horses received one major preferential rank.
idiomatic: On jimao day an edict ordered Heba Sheng, general of the right guard, with one Master of Writing to recruit performers and miscellaneous households for the campaign; on entering service all received substantive posts; men who brought private horses gained one major preferential step.

literal: day gengchen: Attendant, General of the Guard, Prince of Xianyang Tan; General of the Guard, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Nanyang Baoju; Attendant, Pacification-General of the East, Prince of Pingyang Xiu—all were made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On gengchen day Tan, prince of Xianyang, attendant and general of the guard; Baoju, prince of Nanyang, general of the guard and left vice director of the Masters of Writing; and Xiu, prince of Pingyang, attendant and pacification-general of the east, were all made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day yiyou: an edict ordered selection among northerners who had come and among surplus supernumerary officials of the two ministries in the capital.
idiomatic: On yiyou day an edict ordered a purge of supernumerary officials among recent arrivals from the north and surplus staff in the two capital ministries.

literal: day jichou: Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Jing Province Heba Yue was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Regional Inspector of Qi; Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Wei Province Houmochen Yue was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Regional Inspector of Qin.
idiomatic: On jichou day Heba Yue, bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and inspector of Jing, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Qi; Houmochen Yue, bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and inspector of Wei, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Qin.

literal: day gengyin: an edict said that throughout the realm men of virtue, filial piety, benevolence, worth, loyalty, righteousness, resolve, and trust might be summoned to court by ritual invitation; those who did not answer the summons were to be judged disrespectful.
idiomatic: On gengyin day an edict invited men of virtue, filial piety, benevolence, worth, loyalty, righteousness, resolve, and trust throughout the realm to court by ceremonial summons; refusal was to be punished as disrespect.

literal: day bingshen: Liu Lingzhu led his host to camp at Anguo city; Regional Inspector of Ding Province Hou Yuan defeated and beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
idiomatic: On bingshen day Liu Lingzhu encamped at Anguo; Hou Yuan, regional inspector of Ding, routed and killed him and sent his head to the capital.

literal: day wuxu: Bearer of the Staff, Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Husi Chun, and Attendant, General of the Guard Yuan Shou—both were made Special Advance and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On wuxu day Husi Chun, bearer of the staff, attendant, and grand general of chariots and cavalry, and Yuan Shou, attendant and general of the guard, were both made special advance and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: An edict said: "Recently official posts fell out of order and we still ordered a purge; fixed quotas were trimmed and surplus judged—decisions are already rendered."
idiomatic: An edict said: "Official posts have lately fallen into disorder and we ordered a purge; quotas were fixed and surplus cut—judgments are already rendered."

literal: Those cast down may in small measure also be pitied.
idiomatic: Those who fell in the purge deserve some pity as well.

literal: All who were on the purge list may specially receive one preferential rank, all be made generals, enter the selection quota, and be placed according to ability."
idiomatic: All on the purge list shall receive one preferential rank, be made generals, enter the selection rolls, and be placed as their talents allow."

literal: That spring Champion General and Regional Inspector of South Qing Ru Huailang had his subordinate commander He Bao lead three thousand foot and horse to attack Xiao Yan’s garrison commander at Langye and captured Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Cloud-Banner General, and Regional Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces Liu Xiangru.
idiomatic: That spring Ru Huailang, champion general and regional inspector of South Qing, sent his commander He Bao with three thousand foot and horse against Xiao Yan’s garrison at Langye and took Liu Xiangru—left vice director of the Masters of Writing, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, cloud-banner general, and joint inspector of Xu and Yan.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day guimao: the emperor visited the Capital Pavilion in the Hualin Park for archery feast; gifts were distributed in differing measure.
idiomatic: On guimao day in the fourth month of summer the emperor feasted with archery at the Capital Pavilion in Hualin Park; gifts were graded by rank.

literal: The Grand Music Office performed; among the entertainers were buffoons playing idiots; the emperor, because it was not refined amusement, ordered it stopped.
idiomatic: The Grand Music Office performed; some buffoons played the fool. The emperor, finding the show unworthy of court, ordered it stopped.

literal: day renzi: there was service at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
idiomatic: On renzi day the court sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

literal: day guichou: an edict made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan bearer of the staff, attendant, commander of all military affairs of Ji Province, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, grand commander, eastern-route grand mobile office, and regional inspector of Ji; Grand General of Agile Cavalry Prince of Anding Erzhu Zhihu was made commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and regional inspector of Si.
idiomatic: On guichou day an edict made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan bearer of the staff, attendant, commander of Ji military affairs, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, grand commander, eastern-route grand mobile office, and inspector of Ji; Erzhu Zhihu, prince of Anding, grand general of agile cavalry, was made commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Si.

literal: day yimao: General of the Right Guard Heba Sheng and General of the Martial Guard Daye Ba were both made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On yimao day Heba Sheng, general of the right guard, and Daye Ba, general of the martial guard, were both made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day jiwei: at the Xianyang Hall the emperor conducted a selection test of direct-palace scattered cavalier attendants, scattered cavalier attendants, and direct-palace gentlemen; surplus posts held by men without talent were transferred elsewhere.
idiomatic: On jiwei day at Xianyang Hall the emperor tested direct-palace scattered cavalier attendants, scattered cavalier attendants, and direct-palace gentlemen; surplus posts held by unfit men were reassigned.

literal: day guihai: Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang greatly defeated Suqin Mingda, captured him and sent him to the capital, and beheaded him.
idiomatic: On guihai day Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, routed Suqin Mingda, sent him captive to the capital, and had him beheaded.

literal: day bingyin: Attendant and Grand General of Agile Cavalry Erzhu Yanbo was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On bingyin day Erzhu Yanbo, attendant and grand general of agile cavalry, was made minister of works.

literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices not again to call Liang by the name "false"; the statute on fine manufacture was abolished; no ban was placed on traffic with neighboring states.
idiomatic: An edict forbade officials to call the Liang "false" any longer, abolished the fine-manufacture statute, and lifted bans on trade with neighboring states.

literal: An edict [listed] eleven posts—supplementary adviser, infantry commandant, director of imperial carriages, supervisor of the feathered guard, gentleman within the yellow gate, standing-shoot general, court gentleman, palace general, gate gentleman of the palace, supervisor of palace attendants, director of palace attendants, master of rites—who received salary but gave no labor service: those old enough for outside selection followed the regular rule; those not yet old who wished outside selection were permitted to resign.
idiomatic: An edict named eleven posts—from supplementary adviser through master of rites—that drew salary without labor duty: men old enough for outside appointment kept the usual rule; younger men who wished to leave for outside posts might resign.

literal: From the seventh rank upward they entered court on the first and fifteenth of the month; if a regular post was vacant, men were advanced according to talent.
idiomatic: From the seventh rank up, officers attended court on the first and fifteenth; when a regular post fell vacant, talent filled it.

literal: Former supernumeraries who had been purged and given preferential rank had it revoked; those called surplus by circumstance still received one preferential rank.
idiomatic: Former supernumeraries who had gained preferential rank in the purge had it taken back; men still listed as surplus received one preferential step.

literal: Earlier, Administrator of Nanyang Zhao Xiuyan had seized Regional Inspector Li Yanzhi;
idiomatic: Earlier Zhao Xiuyan, administrator of Nanyang, had seized Li Yanzhi the regional inspector;

literal: fifth month, day bingzi: the people of Jing Province city beheaded Xiuyan, sent his head, and in turn set up Yanzhi as regional inspector.
idiomatic: on bingzi day in the fifth month the people of Jing provincial city killed Xiuyan, sent his head, and restored Yanzhi as inspector.

literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent his commander Wei Sengqin and others to attack Cui Zuchi at Dongyang; they captured and beheaded him.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent Wei Sengqin and other commanders against Cui Zuchi at Dongyang and killed him.

literal: sixth month, day gengshen: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, because the Erzhu faction were rebels, first raised the banner of righteous troops at Xindu.
idiomatic: On gengshen day in the sixth month Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, judging the Erzhu clan rebels, first raised righteous troops at Xindu.

literal: He pacified Yin Province in the west, beheaded its regional inspector Erzhu Yusheng, appointed Administrator of South Zhao Commandery Li Yuanzhong regional inspector, and garrisoned Guang’a.
idiomatic: He secured Yin in the west, beheaded Erzhu Yusheng the inspector, made Li Yuanzhong, administrator of South Zhao, inspector, and garrisoned Guang’a.

literal: day guihai: the emperor came to the Xianyang Hall and personally judged wrongful suits.
idiomatic: On guihai day the emperor sat at Xianyang Hall and heard wrongful suits in person.

literal: day wuchen: Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Erzhu Bi was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On wuchen day Erzhu Bi, bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and commissioner with full powers, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: seventh month of autumn, day renshen: Erzhu Shilong and others killed former Grand Guardian Yang Chun, former Minister of Works Yang Jin, and their families.
idiomatic: On renshen day in the seventh month of autumn Erzhu Shilong and his party murdered former grand guardian Yang Chun, former minister of works Yang Jin, and their kin.

literal: day bingxu: Minister of Works Erzhu Yanbo resigned his post because of drought.
idiomatic: On bingxu day Erzhu Yanbo, minister of works, resigned citing drought.

literal: day wuzi: Yanbo was made attendant and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On wuzi day Yanbo was made attendant and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day gengyin: Attendant, Grand Guardian, Commissioner with Full Powers, Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong was made Equal in Honor to the Three Preceptors, [3] ranking below the supreme dukes.
idiomatic: On gengyin day Erzhu Shilong, prince of Leping, attendant, grand guardian, commissioner with full powers, and director of the Masters of Writing, was made equal in honor to the three preceptors, [3] ranking just below the supreme dukes.

literal: eighth month, day gengzi: an edict ordered a universal promotion of three ranks for civil and military under Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang who had gone down to attack Suqin Mingda.
idiomatic: On gengzi day in the eighth month an edict raised three ranks for all civil and military who had followed Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, against Suqin Mingda.

literal: Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao led twenty thousand foot and horse out by Jingxing, hastened toward Yin Province; Li Yuanzhong abandoned the city and returned to Xindu.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, prince of Yingchuan, marched twenty thousand foot and horse through Jingxing toward Yin; Li Yuanzhong abandoned the city and fled back to Xindu.

literal: day bingwu: Prince of Changshan Erzhu Dulu, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, and others led hosts out to resist the banner of righteousness.
idiomatic: On bingwu day Erzhu Dulu, prince of Changshan, Erzhu Zhongyuan, prince of Pengcheng, and others marched out to crush the righteous army.

literal: ninth month, day dingchou: Attendant and Grand General of Agile Cavalry Lu Tong, Grand General of Agile Cavalry Du De, and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Qiao Ning were all made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On dingchou day in the ninth month Lu Tong, attendant and grand general of agile cavalry; Du De, grand general of agile cavalry; and Qiao Ning, grand general of chariots and cavalry, were all made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day jimao: Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all Military Affairs of the Eastern Route, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Eastern-Route Grand Mobile Office, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan was made Grand Mentor.
idiomatic: On jimao day Erzhu Zhongyuan, prince of Pengcheng, bearer of the staff, commander of eastern-route armies, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and eastern-route grand mobile office, was made grand mentor.

literal: day gengchen: Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Commander of all Military Affairs of Guanzhong, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Western-Route Grand Mobile Office, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang was advanced to Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: On gengchen day Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, bearer of the staff, grand general, commander of Guanzhong armies, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and western-route grand mobile office, was advanced to grand marshal.

literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Qing Province, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies Mu Shao died.
idiomatic: Mu Shao, grand general of agile cavalry, regional inspector of Qing, and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, died.
